charts.name: Samoa reference chart of accounts
charts.legal_reference: There is no legal chart of accounts in the texts read for Samoa, and no text read names a standard setter or a framework for company accounts. This chart is original: four digits, blocked so that each range reaches one line of the IFRS-style statements below (IAS 1, expenses by nature), with the accounts a Samoa trading company keeps — VAVAGST output and input tax, import VAVAGST owed to Customs, salary and wages tax withheld, superannuation contributions and withholding taxes payable.

numbering.legal_reference: Value Added Goods and Services Tax Act 2015, s. 33 — a registered person making a taxable supply to another registered person issues the original tax invoice within 28 days of the time of supply, and none is required below $20; s. 39(3) requires copies to be kept. The text read states no document numbering rule, so numbering is `free`; the number format is a convention of this pack.

tax_point.legal_reference: Value Added Goods and Services Tax Act 2015, s. 15(1) — a supply occurs on the earlier of the date the invoice for the supply is issued and the date any payment, part payment included, is made. `invoice_if_issued` states the invoice as the point of the tax where one is issued; a payment received before the invoice brings the supply forward, which the engine does not model for a cash-first sale (see the README). Section 26(2) allows the input tax credit in the GST period in which the input tax is paid, which the engine does not model either.

einvoicing.legal_reference: The Ministry of Revenue runs a Tax Invoice Monitoring System (TIMS) for point-of-sale and electronic sales data devices, announced to vendors in public notices. No structured e-invoice standard or Peppol profile was found, so `obligation` is `none` for a business-to-business e-invoice; the reporting of sales to TIMS is not modelled (see the README).

not_taxed.legal_reference: Value Added Goods and Services Tax Act 2015, s. 8(1)(c) and s. 30 (component B) — a registered person who receives imported services is liable for GST on them and must prepare a recipient-created tax invoice (s. 19(3)); s. 19(2) reduces the value to the proportion for which no input tax credit would be available. A person making only taxable supplies therefore owes and recovers the same amount, and form VAGST 001 has no box for the reverse charge. The pack carries no purchase tax for services bought from abroad: this is a finding about the form read, and the case of a partly exempt person is a gap recorded in the README.
